The industry bears a lot of responsibility here to make sure that when they release things, they’re safe, they’re appropriately vetted, and when things go wrong, you’re going to see us make sure that there’s a very appropriate ongoing notification program so that the government has all the information they need.” “We’re also going to make sure that all the major players outside of technology—critical infrastructure, financial services, energy, oil and gas, all these companies—have the appropriate information they need to make sure that they’ve got plans in place and that we’ve got coordination across things.” “There’s a whole set of laws that the President has mentioned—product liability laws, principal-agent laws, all these things that really govern corporate responsibility in these areas. I think you’re going to see a much greater articulation of that and an indication among the companies that the government has a very clear expectation of their responsibility here.” On enforcement and oversight: “You’re right. That was with a pact that was signed, I guess, a week ago Tuesday with the various players. These are independent auditors. They will report to the board, and all the traditional fiduciary duties and corporate responsibilities will attach to that.”
